title: Select the evidence first
statement: Have students pick out the evidence before they put it in their own words or write about it.
detail: Review feedback on a grade 3 course listed evidence-first articulation among the repairs it asked for. The lesson packet written in response puts evidence selection before paraphrase or written articulation in its required lesson sequence; it is a rule adopted from review, not a result measured here.

evidence.quote: 5. evidence selection before paraphrase or written articulation;
The learner rereads and locates source evidence before interpreting, rehearsing, or composing from it.
EV: Same RT-R3 report, section 2: find-then-write went 0/48 → 45/48 generated lessons; feedback median 24 words (old ~91-word lineage gone); verified by independent recomputation

First, copy-delete is the default a grade 4 child returns to under load, so a task that lets a child paste a long stretch will get a long stretch. Second, and this is the one that bears on our design: the copying is not laziness, it is what the child does when asked to produce prose about a text before the selection has been made.
